Documentation → Releases → 1.6.0

SATOM 1.6.0

Metrics collection reaches FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator and FortiAnalyzer, dashboards gain device pickers, and the published manual and release notes become searchable.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • What's new

  • FortiADC virtual servers
  • FortiAuthenticator identity inventory
  • FortiAnalyzer metrics

Released: 2026-08-07 · All releases

In short#

This release extends fleet metrics beyond FortiWeb. FortiADC virtual servers, the FortiAuthenticator identity inventory and FortiAnalyzer log and storage counters are now collected. Analytics boards gain device and service pickers, so one board can cover the whole fleet. The FortiAuthenticator ADOM now behaves like a full product workspace. The public manual and release notes also become searchable.

What's new#

Monitoring is set up when you save an appliance#

When you save an appliance, SATOM now creates both its metrics collectors and its threshold probes. Until now the threshold probes were only created by Discover, so a device you added through the form had metrics but no thresholds, and nothing told you so.

FortiADC virtual servers#

  • SATOM now collects the runtime state of every FortiADC virtual server.
  • One request covers all the virtual servers in a domain, so a device with 500 virtual servers costs a single round trip.
  • Interface metrics are now collected on FortiADC too.
  • Checked against a live FortiADC running 8.0.3.

FortiAuthenticator identity inventory#

SATOM now counts the identity objects on each FortiAuthenticator: user accounts, groups, tokens, certificates, and RADIUS and TACACS+ clients. Because SATOM fetches only the totals, a directory with 50,000 users costs the same as an empty one.

FortiAnalyzer metrics#

FortiAnalyzer had no metrics collection at all until now. SATOM now collects:

  • log volume and storage
  • alerts and incidents
  • registered devices
  • the task queue

Only counters are collected. SATOM never fetches the content of a log.

Dashboard variables#

Analytics boards can now have variables: pickers at the top of the board that change what every panel shows.

  • One board now covers every device in the fleet, so you no longer need one board per device. Two drill-down boards that use these pickers ship with this release.
  • The service picker depends on the device picker. It offers only the services that exist on the device you selected.

Search on the published manual#

The public documentation site can now be searched. The search covers every published document and every heading inside it (573 headings across 27 documents), so a result takes you straight to the right subsection, not to the top of a long page.

Search across every release#

The public release notes can now be searched across all 226 changelog entries. Each result shows the version it shipped in and links to that release's page. The version list on the left narrows to the releases that contain a match, so you can see at a glance which versions mention what you searched for.

Nine new sections in the user guide#

The user guide gained nine sections on topics it did not cover before:

  • Studio (custom views, plugins and Lua)
  • High availability
  • AppIDs
  • a tab-by-tab Settings reference
  • log collection and offline backup import
  • system provisioning profiles and baselines
  • the template library and section catalog
  • the endpoint registry and API explorer
  • release notes

The manual grew from 23 to 32 sections, and it now tells you where to read what changed in each version.

What changes for you#

  • The release notes show a list of versions and one version's details. Versions are listed on the left, newest first, and the selected version's changes appear on the right. The page opens on the version you are running. Every version page has the full list, so you can jump between versions without scrolling through the whole changelog.
  • Wider manual and release notes on large screens. On screens wider than 1400 pixels, the manual and release notes now use 80% of the screen width. Smaller screens keep the previous width, because 80% of a smaller screen would be narrower than before.
  • Lua Studio is gone from the FortiAuthenticator ADOM. FortiAuthenticator has nothing that runs scripts, so the page listed no targets and no devices. Lua Studio is still available for FortiWeb and FortiADC.
  • Your ADOM settings take priority over the factory defaults. If an administrator turned on a capability for an ADOM in Settings → ADOMs, SATOM keeps it. In the FortiAuthenticator ADOM this means the firmware library opens if it was enabled there. Naming and the Regex lab still send you out of that workspace.

Fixed#

  • Device names could appear on the public documentation site. The rule that hid appliance names when the manual was published only knew the devices that existed on the day it was written, so devices added later were no longer hidden. The rule now matches any device name built from a product name followed by a number, so new devices are covered as soon as you add them. Plain product names stay visible.
  • Analytics boards failed with an error when a device or policy name contained a hyphen, which is almost every name. Boards now load normally with these names.
  • Opening the FortiAuthenticator ADOM took you to the FortiWeb home page. This happened from the product picker, the sidebar and the device list, and it kept your session in FortiWeb. Before this fix, the only way into the FortiAuthenticator workspace was to type its address.
  • The Global home page showed only FortiWeb and FortiADC. FortiAuthenticator and FortiAnalyzer units were missing from the console that is meant to show the whole fleet. The cards and the fleet table now include every product SATOM manages, so a new product appears automatically. Devices that belong to no active ADOM are listed too.
  • An ADOM that still had appliances could be deleted. Its devices stayed in the list but no console could reach them. You can no longer delete an ADOM that has at least one appliance. The refusal tells you why and how many appliances are in the way.
  • The FortiAuthenticator ADOM was missing the search icon in the top bar and its link in the device list.
  • The manual sidebar showed text like &amp;amp; in place of & in some headings.

Under the hood#

  • Service Monitor stays. Its checks overlap with the new collectors, but only Service Monitor can raise the alert for "every backend behind this policy is down". It stays in place until alerting can work from the collected metrics.
  • FortiAnalyzer collection has not been tested on real hardware, because none was reachable. If the device returns data in a shape SATOM does not recognise, SATOM records nothing rather than a number that looks plausible but is wrong.
  • A tool that builds the field catalog had a list of reference appliances written into it. You now configure its sources yourself, and it refuses to run until you do.
